# Dairee

> Dairee is a student-led startup from Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada, developing a dry powder plant fertilizer made from milk, eggshells and potato peels that would otherwise be wasted. It is designed for houseplants and home gardens. Dairee is in development and not yet for sale.

## Key facts
- Name: Dairee
- Website: https://dairee.ca
- What: A dry powder fertilizer for houseplants and home gardens, mixed into soil or sprinkled on top
- Ingredients: Milk, eggshells and potato peels that would otherwise be thrown away, dried and ground into one powder
- Format history: Dairee first explored a liquid fertilizer, then moved to a dry powder
- Where: Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada
- Started at: Saint Mary's University (SMU), Halifax
- Founders: Poojan Pitolwala (Founder & CEO), Sophie Wells (Chief Operating Officer), Keegan Purnell (Chief Marketing Officer)
- Stage: Building and testing the first batches of powder; progressing in the SMU Innovation Cup
- Status: Not for sale. Formulation and performance have not yet been validated, and Dairee makes no performance claims.
- Contact: getdairee@gmail.com
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/getdairee/
- Tagline: Good things deserve to grow again.

## Why these ingredients
Gardeners have added milk, crushed eggshells and potato peels to soil for generations, but there is little careful testing behind it. Dairee is investigating what each one adds:
- Milk: calcium, plus protein that releases nitrogen as it breaks down in soil
- Eggshells: mostly calcium carbonate, a slow-release source of calcium
- Potato peels: potassium, with small amounts of phosphorus
Drying the ingredients into a powder may help with smell, mould and shelf life; that is one of the first things Dairee is testing.

## Development path
1. Recover: find sources of milk, eggshells and potato peels that would otherwise be thrown away.
2. Formulate: dry, grind and blend the three ingredients into a powder (current stage).
3. Evaluate: test nutrient content, moisture, odour and plant response, and share results.
4. Grow: pilot with Nova Scotia gardeners only if the evidence holds up.

## How to help
- Follow progress on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/getdairee/
- Gardeners who want to test an early batch can email getdairee@gmail.com
- Dairies, bakeries, restaurants, cafés, farms and grocers in Nova Scotia with surplus milk, eggshells or potato peels can email getdairee@gmail.com
